title: Definition
text: $$\tan\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$$ is the slope of the line connecting the origin to the point on the unit circle at $$\left(\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right), \sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right).$$\n##figure7.gif##

figureAlts.figure7.gif: Diagram of the coordinate (cosine of negative pi over 3, sine of negative pi over 3) on the unit circle. The point is located five-sixths of the way around the circumference of the entire circle in the fourth quadrant. The angle between the positive horizontal axis and the line from the origin to the point going clockwise is negative pi over 3 radians.
